summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease, was admitted for volume overload characterized by 20-pound weight gain, lower extremity edema, and rising creatinine. He was treated with IV furosemide, transitioned to oral diuretics, and later had them held due to over-diuresis. A pericardial effusion was noted on echocardiogram but showed no hemodynamic compromise. Fat pad and bone marrow biopsies were performed; amyloidosis was ruled out. He developed a C. difficile infection, treated with oral vancomycin. His weight decreased to 193 pounds, renal function stabilized with creatinine around 4.0, and he improved clinically. He was discharged home with services, on a full course of vancomycin, with instructions to hold diuretics until outpatient follow-up.
